question: Should onboarding fees be one-time or amortized into ARR?
answer:
**Direct Answer:** One-time fees for implementation cost >$15k, no amortization. ARR capture kills NRR; one-time fees preserve gross margin and align incentives. For <$5k onboarding, include in monthly pricing. For $5–15k, charge separately but do not capitalize as deferred revenue. **The Detail** Many finance teams incorrectly amortize onboarding into ARR to inflate reported growth. This destroys NRR transparency and hides true unit economics. **Comparison:** | Approach | Pros | Cons | Use Case | |----------|------|------|----------| | One-time fee | True ARR visibility, margin-protective, cash upfront | Sales friction on large deals | Deals >$15k impl cost | | Amortized to ARR | Smoother revenue recognition, smaller initial payment | Inflates growth, masks churn, destroys NRR | Small deals <$5k | | Monthly add-on | Simple billing, upsell floor | Customer sticker-shock, finance complexity | Mid-market $5–15k | **Math impact (Example: $100k deal, $20k onboarding):** **Option A: One-time fee** - Year 1 ARR: $100k (clean) - Year 2 ARR: $105k (5% NRR, no onboarding noise) - CAC payback: 10 months (using $100k as denominator) - Gross margin: $20k upfront + $75k recurring margins year 1 = 95% blended **Option B: Amortize over 12 months** - Year 1 ARR: $101.67k (distorted; $20k ÷ 12 = $1.67k/mo added) - Year 2: $105k (renewal, no onboarding layer) - Net Retention: 103.3% (phantom number; not real) - Conceals true unit economics **Implementation rules:** 1. **Separate line items on contracts** — Onboarding, implementation, custom dev are NOT ARR. Use GL codes that don't flow to ARR. 2. **Cash accounting, not accrual** — Revenue-recognize onboarding fees when delivery completes, not over contract term. SaaS audit standards (KPMG, EY) accept this. 3. **Sales comp incentive clarity** — Align AE bonuses to ARR only (not implementation fees). Prevents AEs from loading fake services. 4. **Professional services org isolation** — If services are <20% revenue margin, run as cost center; if >30%, treat as separate P&L. Cap implementation at 15–20% of first-year contract value. 5. **Customer success handoff** — CS owns "time-to-value" outcome, not implementation revenue. Separate KPIs. **Red flags:** - Implementation fees >25% of first-year ARR - Amortized fees exceeding 5% of recurring revenue - Services margin <20% ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Deal Structure"] --> B{"Impl Cost?"} B -->|"<$5k"| C["Include in Monthly Pricing"] B -->|"$5-15k"| D["Monthly Add-on
